IQE's permanent CEO as of 13 May 2025 is Jutta Meier, who also holds the CFO portfolio. The prep data appears to have contained an erroneous name. Chapter heading should be updated to reflect the actual leadership.

chapters.title: Qorvo, Lumentum, Coherent, and the foundry-and-substrate supply chain
chapters.body:
## A Merchant Foundry at the Centre of the Stack

IQE plc sits at a specific and structurally irreplaceable position in the compound semiconductor value chain: it grows the epitaxial layers onto which every downstream device manufacturer then fabricates their circuits. That positioning makes IQE's customer list a who's-who of the compound semiconductor device world — but it also concentrates the company's revenue fortunes in the hands of a small number of large buyers, each of which carries its own demand cycle.

The customer base divides cleanly into two revenue streams. Wireless and RF account for the larger share in aggregate across IQE's history: Qorvo, Broadcom, Skyworks Solutions, and Murata purchase gallium arsenide epitaxial wafers that become the power amplifiers in smartphone handsets and 5G base stations. Photonics — indium phosphide for datacom and telecom transceivers, and VCSEL structures for sensing and short-reach optical links — is the faster-growing segment and the one that now underpins the company's medium-term investment thesis.

## The RF Customer Base: GaAs and the 5G Amplifier Supply Chain

The GaAs RF business is IQE's most mature revenue line. Qorvo, formed from the 2015 merger of RF Micro Devices and TriQuint Semiconductor, is the largest standalone RF chip company in the world by revenue and one of IQE's most important customers. Broadcom's wireless connectivity and RF front-end division and Skyworks Solutions complete a triad of high-volume fabless GaAs device companies that source epi wafers predominantly from merchant suppliers including IQE. Murata, the Japanese passive-component and module giant, rounds out the tier-one RF customer set through its RF module operations.

These customers are not passive purchasers. Qorvo and Skyworks in particular maintain long-term supply relationships that involve technical qualification cycles — a compound semiconductor epi layer must be qualified against a device company's own process design kit before volume shipments begin — which create switching costs on both sides. IQE's ability to maintain qualification across multiple device geometries and GaAs alloy compositions at the Bethlehem, Pennsylvania facility has been a structural advantage. The Bethlehem site, opened in 2018 as one of the largest compound semiconductor epi facilities globally at roughly 200,000 square feet, was dimensioned for the 5G ramp that the industry anticipated through 2019 and 2020. The actual volume trajectory proved more modest through the 2022-2024 downcycle, leaving Bethlehem carrying meaningful idle capacity.

Smartphone unit volume and the pace of 5G handset penetration in China are the proximate demand drivers for GaAs RF epi. The 2022-2024 period saw both: post-pandemic inventory corrections compressed GaAs wafer orders across the supply chain, and the US-China technology trade restrictions introduced uncertainty about the China RF handset supply chain that cascaded into IQE's order book. IQE's reported revenue fell from £167.3 million in 2022 to £115.3 million in 2023, a decline that reflected both the RF downturn and the post-peak normalisation of VCSEL volumes.

## Lumentum, Coherent, and the VCSEL Decade

The photonics customer story has two chapters. The first, spanning roughly 2017 to 2021, was written almost entirely by Apple.

Lumentum Holdings became IQE's most significant photonics customer as it won the VCSEL supply contract for Apple's Face ID system, introduced with the iPhone X in late 2017. Lumentum sourced VCSEL epitaxial wafers from IQE's Taunton, Massachusetts facility — the former Kopin compound semiconductor site that IQE had acquired in 2018 specifically to add capacity for what it correctly anticipated would be a high-volume 3D sensing demand wave. The Face ID supply chain briefly made IQE one of the more prominent beneficiaries of Apple's compound semiconductor spend, with revenue lifting to £178 million in 2020 as VCSEL volumes peaked. Coherent — then still operating under the II-VI Incorporated name before the 2022 merger with Coherent Corp. — was a secondary VCSEL customer through the same period.

The Apple VCSEL volume normalised sharply after 2020 as Apple diversified its VCSEL supplier base and as the incremental content per device stabilised. IQE's Taunton mega-facility, designed to serve peak VCSEL demand, carried the cost of under-utilisation through 2022 and 2023. The facility's square footage — multiple hundreds of thousands of square feet across what had been Kopin's high-volume III-V manufacturing floors — translated into fixed costs that compressed operating margins during the period of volume reduction.

The second chapter of the photonics story is being written by data centre optical interconnect. Lumentum and Coherent are now among the principal suppliers of 400G, 800G, and emerging 1.6T optical transceivers consumed in hyperscale data centre builds by Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta. Those transceivers are built on indium phosphide epitaxial wafers. Coherent in particular has invested aggressively in vertical integration of InP photonics manufacturing — its indium phosphide laser and modulator chips sit at the core of its data centre transceiver portfolio — and IQE's InP epi business supports that supply chain. Marvell Technology, through the Inphi acquisition completed in 2021, has become a significant InP-based photonic integrated circuit customer aligned to the same AI infrastructure demand.

IQE does not sell directly to the hyperscalers. The revenue path runs: IQE epi wafer → Lumentum or Coherent device fabrication → transceiver module → hyperscaler data centre. But the AI-driven capital expenditure cycle at Microsoft, Google, and Meta is nonetheless the structural demand signal that is pulling through IQE's InP order book. The constraint in 2024 and into 2025 was not demand — it was InP substrate supply. Indium phosphide bulk wafers, on which IQE grows its epi, are a more constrained supply chain than GaAs. Principal substrate suppliers include Sumitomo Electric, which operates one of the largest InP wafer businesses globally, along with AXT Inc. and a smaller group of European and Asian producers. Tight InP substrate availability through the 2024-2025 period acted as a ceiling on how quickly IQE could ramp InP epi output in response to strengthening transceiver demand.

## Foundry Partners and the Broader Customer Architecture

TSMC and GlobalFoundries represent a distinct customer category: compound semiconductor foundries that run specific process flows — GaN-on-silicon, SiGe, and select III-V processes — and source epi material from IQE as a specialist input. These relationships are more technically specific than the device company relationships, involving detailed process integration rather than commodity wafer supply, and they carry long qualification cycles that create durable revenue.

IQE's Singapore operations were established in part to serve the Asian foundry ecosystem, with proximity to TSMC's primary wafer fabs and the broader Hsinchu semiconductor cluster providing logistical advantage. The Taiwan joint-venture-anchored presence supports that same cluster.

## Upstream: Substrates, Chemicals, and Reactors

IQE's own supply chain contains several constraints worth noting. The company is a significant consumer of metalorganic precursor chemicals — trimethylgallium, trimethylindium, trimethylaluminium, and related compounds — consumed in the metalorganic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD) reactors that grow the epi layers. These precursors are produced by a small number of specialty chemical suppliers; supply continuity and pricing are material inputs to IQE's cost structure.

The MOCVD reactor fleet itself represents a concentrated equipment dependency. Aixtron SE and Veeco Instruments are the two principal MOCVD reactor manufacturers globally. Aixtron, listed in Frankfurt, dominates the high-volume III-V MOCVD market; Veeco has significant presence in VCSEL and power device epi. IQE's reactor base spans both vendors. New reactor lead times — which in peak-demand periods have extended to twelve months or more — mean that capacity additions require long planning horizons, a structural feature that gives IQE limited short-term flexibility to respond to demand step-changes. MBE, or molecular beam epitaxy, equipment from Veeco and other suppliers serves IQE's more specialised research and lower-volume device lines.

On the substrate side, GaAs wafers are sourced from Freiberger Compound Materials, a German producer, and AXT Inc., along with Sumitomo and others. The GaAs substrate supply chain is considerably more developed and less constrained than InP, reflecting decades of volume production for the GaAs RF industry.

## Geographic Exposure and Trade Policy

IQE's operational geography maps onto the compound semiconductor industry's policy fault lines. UK operations benefit from the UK's industrial strategy frameworks supporting semiconductor self-sufficiency — a priority that intensified post-Brexit and in response to the global chip shortage of 2021-2022. US operations in Pennsylvania and Massachusetts sit within the scope of the CHIPS and Science Act framework, which allocated capital toward domestic compound semiconductor manufacturing. The tension between US-China technology export controls and IQE's Asian customer base — particularly in Taiwan, where the foundry ecosystem includes companies with mainland China exposure — introduces a geopolitical dimension to what is otherwise a materials supply business. As of the frozen window, IQE had not disclosed material direct China revenue, but the indirect exposure through RF handset customers with China supply chains was a live commercial variable through the 2023-2025 period.

chapters.title: Where IQE sits in compound semiconductor epitaxy
chapters.body:
## The merchant model in a fragmented industry

Compound semiconductor epitaxy is not a market with a single dominant structure. It is divided, instead, into three overlapping supply modes that compete for the same device customers and, increasingly, for the same end applications. The first is merchant epitaxy: independent foundries that grow specialised wafers and sell them to fabless or lightly-integrated device manufacturers. The second is captive epitaxy embedded inside integrated device manufacturers — IDMs that grow their own epi as a feedstock for the chips they sell downstream. The third is foundry-internal epi, where advanced foundries such as TSMC operate compound semiconductor process flows as part of broader platform strategies. IQE plc occupied the apex of the merchant segment, by breadth of material systems mastered and by global facility scale, at the snapshot date of May 2026. Understanding its competitive position requires mapping all three supply modes and the structural forces that shift volume between them.

The merchant epi model exists because compound semiconductor device manufacturers often lack the capital, the materials science expertise, or the volume to justify internalising epitaxial growth. Unlike silicon, where the substrate is a commodity and a high-school physics student can describe the doping mechanism, compound semiconductor epi requires precision control of layer thickness, composition, and doping profile across material systems — GaAs, InP, GaN, GaSb, and their alloys — that each demand separate reactor chemistries, substrate handling, and characterisation methodologies. A GaAs MOCVD reactor configured for 5G power-amplifier heterojunction bipolar transistors is not simply reprogrammed to grow InP distributed feedback laser structures. This materials complexity is the structural reason the merchant model exists, and the structural reason IQE accumulated scale across material systems rather than concentrating in one.

## IQE's unmatched breadth among independent suppliers

At the snapshot date, IQE was the only independent merchant epi supplier operating at commercial scale across all principal III-V and related material systems simultaneously: gallium arsenide for 5G RF and microwave devices; indium phosphide for datacom and telecom optical transceivers and, most recently, AI data centre interconnect; gallium nitride for power electronics and RF; VCSEL epi stacks for 3D sensing and datacom; and silicon-germanium for high-speed electronics. That breadth is not replicated by any competitor in the merchant segment.

The principal independent merchant peers at scale were both Taiwanese. Visual Photonics Epitaxy Company — known in the industry as VPEC — and Landmark Optoelectronics operated meaningful epi capacity, primarily concentrated in GaAs and InP for the datacom and telecom photonics markets. Both companies had close structural ties to Taiwan's dense photonics supply chain, offering geographic convenience to Taiwan-based device manufacturers. Neither operated the material system breadth of IQE, and neither had approached IQE's global facility footprint. Their competitive strength was specificity and supply-chain proximity within the Taiwan–Asia photonics cluster, not breadth or independent scale.

IQE's own facility footprint was genuinely global by the snapshot date. The Cardiff headquarters anchored European operations; Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, housed what had historically been among the largest compound semiconductor epi facilities globally; the Taunton, Massachusetts site, acquired in 2018 from Kopin Corporation, provided dedicated VCSEL capacity at the scale demanded by the Apple Face ID production ramp; Singapore and a Taiwan joint-venture operation supported the Asian foundry ecosystem. That geography was not accidental — it mapped to IQE's principal customer concentrations, serving Qorvo, Broadcom, Skyworks Solutions, and Murata on the 5G RF GaAs side, and Lumentum, Coherent, and Marvell-Inphi on the datacom photonics InP side.

## Captive epi at IDMs: the permanent structural pressure

Captive epitaxy inside integrated device manufacturers is the most enduring structural competitive pressure IQE faces — not a cyclical disruption but a permanent feature of the industry architecture. When an IDM controls both epi growth and downstream device processing, it can optimise the entire stack for yield and performance in ways a merchant supplier can approximate but not guarantee. The IDM also internalises the epi margin, reducing total cost of ownership at sufficient volume.

Sumitomo Electric Industries was the most consequential captive epi competitor in the material system most critical to IQE's forward strategy. Sumitomo operated substantial InP epitaxial capacity internally, serving its own optical component manufacturing. In the AI photonics era — where InP is the preferred material for high-speed electro-optic modulators and integrated photonic circuits in data centre interconnect — Sumitomo's captive InP epi position placed it at the centre of the same demand surge IQE was pursuing from the merchant side. This dynamic, IQE as merchant InP supplier against Sumitomo as captive InP grower, defined the principal strategic competitive question in the InP photonics franchise through the snapshot window.

Coherent, the compound semiconductor and laser giant formed from the merger of II-VI Incorporated and Coherent Corp., represented the second major captive epi concentration. Post-merger, Coherent operated substantial internal VCSEL epi capacity as well as broader compound semiconductor epitaxial capability across GaAs and InP material systems. Given that Coherent's device business competed directly in datacom transceivers and optical modules — the very products driving the AI data centre optical interconnect build-out — Coherent's captive epi position was both a direct operational competitor to IQE's merchant supply and, simultaneously, a customer in product lines where Coherent sourced externally. That dual customer–competitor dynamic was not unique to Coherent in this industry, but its scale made it particularly consequential for IQE's strategic planning.

## Foundry-internal compound semiconductor: a contained compression

The third competitive mode — foundry-internal compound semiconductor flows — operated at the intersection of compound semiconductors and advanced silicon logic foundry strategy. TSMC operated compound semiconductor process technologies as part of its portfolio of specialty process flows, serving specific device segments where tight integration with digital silicon provided a system-level advantage. GlobalFoundries operated RF GaN process flows as part of its US defence and commercial semiconductor offering. Neither TSMC nor GlobalFoundries was a merchant epi supplier in the IQE sense — their compound semiconductor flows served their own wafer fabrication customers within a closed process ecosystem. But they represented a structural compression on the addressable merchant epi market: to the extent a device designer chose a foundry-internal compound semiconductor flow, that epi volume was captured inside the foundry and never reached the merchant market.

The compression effect was material but bounded. Foundry-internal compound semiconductor flows could not replicate the full material breadth of an independent merchant: TSMC's compound semiconductor offering was not, at the snapshot date, a substitute for InP photonics epi or GaN-on-SiC power epi at IQE's specification range. The competitive risk was architectural displacement at the device customer level over a multi-year horizon, not an immediate volume loss.

## The InP arena and the AI photonics inflection

The structural competitive question that most preoccupied IQE's strategic posture through the snapshot period was not displacement by foundries but the volume allocation decision inside hyperscale data centre optical interconnect. AI training and inference at scale required large numbers of high-speed optical transceivers — co-packaged optics and pluggable modules — in which InP electro-optic components operated at speeds that silicon photonics could not yet match across all performance axes. That demand represented a genuine step-change for InP epi.

The contest for that InP volume ran along a single axis: how much would flow to merchant epi suppliers like IQE, and how much would be captured by captive InP growers at the IDMs building those transceivers? Sumitomo Electric's vertically integrated optical component business was the most prominent captive competitor in this contest. A hyperscale customer sourcing 400G or 800G transceivers from a vertically integrated Sumitomo supply chain would not generate InP epi demand for IQE. A hyperscale customer sourcing from an InP photonic integrated circuit supplier without captive epi — or from a supplier deliberately keeping IQE in the supply chain as a second source — would.

| Supply model | Principal players | InP photonics exposure | Breadth of material systems |
|---|---|---|---|
| Merchant (independent) | IQE (largest), VPEC, Landmark | High — merchant InP for transceiver epi | IQE: full III-V breadth; VPEC/Landmark: primarily GaAs/InP |
| Captive IDM | Sumitomo Electric, Coherent | High — internal InP for optical devices | Single-system depth, not merchant breadth |
| Foundry-internal | TSMC, GlobalFoundries | Limited at snapshot date | Platform-specific flows |

IQE's strategic argument for merchant supply in this environment rested on two planks. The first was second-sourcing logic: device manufacturers with high-volume InP requirements had structural incentives to maintain non-captive supply options to avoid dependence on a single integrated competitor. The second was material flexibility: IQE's breadth across GaAs, InP, GaN, and VCSEL material systems meant a photonics customer could consolidate epi sourcing across multiple device types with a single merchant supplier, reducing qualification burden. Whether those arguments translated into sustained volume gains in the AI photonics cycle was the forward-looking competitive test that the snapshot period left unanswered.

chapters.title: From the 2018 Bethlehem opening to the 2024 CEO reset and the InP inflection
chapters.body:
## The Bethlehem Bet

The compound semiconductor industry rarely builds ahead of demand. IQE plc broke that convention in 2018 when it opened its Bethlehem, Pennsylvania facility — a 200,000 square-foot epiwafer manufacturing complex that represented one of the largest dedicated compound semiconductor epitaxy sites in North America and a direct capital commitment to what the Cardiff-based group believed was a structural inflection in photonics volume.

The strategic logic was legible even then. Apple had launched the iPhone X in September 2017, embedding a Face ID dot projector that fired 30,000 infrared points across a user's face sixty times per second. Each dot projector consumed vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser — VCSEL — epiwafers. IQE, as a principal supplier of VCSEL epi through customers including Lumentum, had found itself at the epicentre of a consumer electronics super-cycle it had spent years positioning to serve.

The group had listed on AIM in 2000, nearly three decades after its 1988 founding in Cardiff by researchers commercialising III-V semiconductor growth expertise from the University of Wales. Through the 2000s and 2010s it had quietly assembled global epi capacity across Wales, the US, and Singapore, serving RF compound semiconductors for cellular handsets and base stations alongside its photonics lines. The iPhone X was the moment the photonics thesis arrived at scale.

## The VCSEL Cycle and Its Unwind

Revenue tells the story efficiently.

| Fiscal Year | Revenue (£m) | Key Driver |
|-------------|-------------|-----------|
| 2019 | 140.0 | VCSEL ramp continuing |
| 2020 | 178.0 | Peak VCSEL volume |
| 2021 | 154.0 | Post-peak normalisation begins |
| 2022 | 167.0 | Partial recovery, RF contribution |
| 2023 | 115.3 | Revenue compression, under-utilisation |

The 2020 peak at £178m reflected a period in which IQE's capital expenditure decisions — including Bethlehem and the 2018 acquisition of Kopin Corporation's Taunton, Massachusetts compound semiconductor facility — appeared well timed. Taunton, a multi-hundred-thousand square-foot site positioned as a mega-facility for scaled epi production, expanded the group's US manufacturing footprint at precisely the moment US-based photonics customers were accelerating their own supply chain commitments.

The unwind that followed was severe. By 2023, revenue had compressed to £115.3m — a 35 per cent decline from the 2020 peak. The underlying mechanism was not technology substitution but demand cycle: Apple's VCSEL consumption normalised as Face ID became a standard component rather than a product launch catalyst, the growth curve flattening against the fixed-cost base IQE had installed to serve the peak. Bethlehem and Taunton, sized for a volume trajectory that did not materialise as expected, carried significant idle epi reactor capacity through 2022 and into 2023. For a business whose gross margins are structurally sensitive to facility utilisation — epi reactors are expensive assets that produce revenue only when running — idle capacity translates directly into operating losses.

## Lemos and the Restructuring Imperative

Against this backdrop, the board appointed Americo Lemos as chief executive in February 2022. His arrival signalled a deliberate shift in operational emphasis: Lemos came not from within the compound semiconductor epi world but from GlobalFoundries, where he had served as senior vice president of manufacturing. The choice of an executive with a large-scale semiconductor manufacturing background — accustomed to driving utilisation, operational efficiency, and discipline across capital-intensive fab networks — reflected a board view that IQE's near-term challenge was as much operational as it was commercial.

Lemos spent his tenure attempting to restructure the cost base, refine the customer portfolio, and articulate a coherent strategic narrative around IQE's multiple end markets: RF compound semiconductors for smartphones and 5G base stations; photonics for datacom, telecom, and sensing; power electronics; and advanced sensing applications including automotive LiDAR. The argument, consistent through his period, was that IQE's pure-play position in compound semiconductor epitaxy gave it structural exposure across each of these demand vectors — that the same epi growth capability serving a VCSEL line could be redeployed toward InP for optical transceivers or GaN for power devices as market conditions shifted.

The execution challenge was proving that redeployment thesis while the principal revenue base — RF and VCSEL photonics — remained under cyclical pressure. The 2023 revenue figure of £115.3m represented the sharpest compression of the Lemos period, a number that made the optimistic case for the multi-market strategy harder to sustain against investor scrutiny.

## October 2024: The Board Acts

In October 2024, Lemos stepped down. The board's announcement via London Stock Exchange RNS marked the end of a thirty-two-month tenure that had stabilised the business operationally without fully resolving the revenue growth question. Non-executive chair Chris Meadows assumed an active operational steering role through the transition. CFO Jutta Meier, long-tenured across multiple IQE CEO transitions, provided the financial and operational continuity the group needed through an extended interim period.

The 2024 CEO departure is best understood not as a repudiation of the strategic direction — the InP photonics thesis, the multi-market exposure argument, the Bethlehem and Taunton long-cycle bet — but as a board judgement that execution velocity needed to accelerate. The compound semiconductor capital cycle does not wait: 800G optical transceivers were entering volume deployment across hyperscale data centres, 1.6T platforms were moving from specification to early production, and each transceiver consumed meaningful InP epiwafer area per unit. IQE's epi capacity, if it could be commercially engaged at scale, was positioned for exactly this demand pull.

## Steve Smith and the InP Inflection

Steve Smith was appointed permanent chief executive in 2025, closing the interim period. Confirmation of his precise appointment date and prior executive background should be drawn from the relevant IQE RNS announcement and current investor relations communications at iqep.com; the prep data available at the frozen snapshot date of 23 May 2026 identifies the appointment but does not surface verbatim RNS citation or full biographical detail for independent verification here.

What the Smith appointment context makes clear is the strategic frame under which he assumed the role. The AI infrastructure build-out — hyperscale data centres requiring optical interconnect at 800G and 1.6T speeds to support GPU cluster networking — was generating the first sustained demand signal for InP epiwafers that IQE's facilities were structured to supply. InP is the substrate of choice for high-speed indium phosphide photonic integrated circuits underpinning coherent optical transceivers at these speeds. Unlike the VCSEL cycle, which was principally a consumer electronics volume story, the InP/AI data centre thesis is a capital infrastructure story with longer demand visibility and higher per-unit epi content.

The 5G RF cycle provided a parallel demand thread. GaAs and GaN epi for smartphone and base station RF front-end modules had remained a steady contributor through the VCSEL unwind; the maturing 5G rollout and early positioning for Advanced 5G and 6G RF architectures gave IQE a base load against which to absorb fixed costs as the photonics opportunity developed.

Automotive LiDAR represented a third vector: VCSEL arrays for long-range sensing in advanced driver assistance systems and autonomous vehicles consumed epi area in ways structurally similar to consumer VCSEL but with longer design-in cycles and less consumer-cycle volatility.

## Specialist Commentary

Specialist commentary framing of IQE by Aleabit was not surfaced in the bounded primary-source set used for this dossier. Retail investor discussion on X (formerly Twitter) through 2023 and 2024 centred on the VCSEL-cycle disappointment and the gap between IQE's articulated multi-market strategic positioning and the revenue line that materialised. The most frequently recurring observation among technically literate commentators was the under-utilisation problem at Bethlehem and Taunton — characterising it as a fixed-cost trap that would require sustained demand, not merely improved commercial pipeline, to resolve. As the InP data-centre narrative gained specificity through 2024 and into 2025, retail commentary tone shifted toward cautious re-engagement with the forward thesis, though scepticism about execution timeline remained.

## Forward Catalysts at the Snapshot Date

From the frozen snapshot of 23 May 2026, the forward catalyst set for IQE includes the 2026 half-year results, the most recent full-year annual report, and the evolving InP photonics demand data from the optical transceiver supply chain. LightCounting and other specialist optical networking research groups have documented the pace of 800G transceiver deployment and the forward trajectory for 1.6T; IQE's ability to translate that demand signal into booked epi revenue — and into Bethlehem and Taunton utilisation rates that structurally improve gross margin — is the quantitative test of the Smith-era strategic thesis. The 5G RF cycle trajectory and the scaling of automotive VCSEL LiDAR programmes represent secondary catalysts. The trajectory from the 2018 Bethlehem opening to the 2026 snapshot is, in summary, a story of correctly anticipating a structural demand shift but encountering the timing risk inherent in capital-intensive pure-play positioning: the capacity arrived; the demand arrival is the variable still being resolved.

chapters.title: Epitaxy science, reactor IP, material-system breadth
chapters.body:
## The Science at the Core

Epitaxy is the art of growing crystalline semiconductor layers one atomic plane at a time, with composition, thickness, and doping controlled to tolerances measured in nanometres. For compound semiconductors, this is not chemistry that can be replicated by a device manufacturer as an afterthought to chip design. It requires decades of accumulated process knowledge, proprietary reactor configurations, and recipe libraries that represent the actual competitive barrier in the industry. IQE plc, since its 1988 founding in Cardiff by Professor Philip Blood and colleagues from the then-active university research group, built its market position not as a wafer commodity supplier but as a precision-science organisation whose stock-in-trade was recipe development and process repeatability at production scale.

The company operated both principal epitaxial deposition methods. Metal-organic chemical vapour deposition — MOCVD — dominated the commercial production base, deploying organometallic precursors in a controlled gas-phase reaction across heated substrates inside purpose-engineered reactor chambers. Molecular beam epitaxy — MBE — provided a complementary capability: slower throughput but exceptional compositional precision, suited to research-grade structures and device families where material quality tolerances were at the frontier of what any process could achieve. IQE maintained both technologies across its global manufacturing estate, positioning itself to serve customers whose device roadmaps moved between the two techniques as volume and specification requirements evolved.

## Material Systems and Recipe Portfolios

The breadth of IQE's material-system coverage was, by the mid-2020s, a genuine differentiating asset. Most compound semiconductor epi suppliers had gravitated toward one or two material families. IQE maintained commercial-scale production capability across five principal systems, each requiring distinct reactor chemistry, substrate handling protocols, and defect-management expertise.

Gallium arsenide remained the highest-volume materials platform measured by wafer throughput, anchored in the 5G RF amplifier supply chain. GaAs pHEMT and HBT epi structures powered the power-amplifier die at the heart of every smartphone RF front-end module. Customers including Qorvo, Broadcom, and Skyworks Solutions demanded epi wafers with defect densities, surface morphology, and layer thickness uniformity meeting specifications that left little margin for process drift. IQE's GaAs recipe portfolio — developed and refined over three decades of production — represented a catalogue of device-specific growth recipes that could not be recreated quickly by a new entrant.

Indium phosphide was the material system attracting the sharpest investor attention as the AI infrastructure build-out accelerated. InP's direct bandgap and electron mobility characteristics made it the foundational material for high-speed optical modulators and lasers operating at the 1310nm and 1550nm wavelengths that dominated fibre-optic datacom. The device structures of consequence for AI data centre optical interconnect — directly modulated lasers, electro-absorption modulated lasers, and coherent transceiver chips integrating both modulation and detection functions — required InP epi stacks of considerable complexity. A coherent 400G or 800G transceiver demanded epitaxial structures with multiple active and passive layer sequences grown in sequence, lattice-matched throughout, with defect densities controlled to preserve optical gain and modal behaviour. Recipe development cycles for new coherent device structures routinely extended to eighteen months or longer, encompassing growth optimisation, material characterisation, device iteration, and reliability screening. That development timeline, and the process knowledge embedded in it, constituted IQE's core IP for the InP photonics segment.

Gallium nitride on silicon carbide substrates served the 5G infrastructure RF market — base-station power amplifiers requiring higher power density and efficiency than GaAs could deliver. GaN epi growth demanded precise control of dislocation densities arising from the lattice mismatch between the GaN epilayer and the SiC substrate; buffer layer engineering to manage this mismatch was the central process-IP challenge, and IQE had developed its own buffer architectures over a multi-year programme.

Silicon-germanium epitaxy occupied a distinct niche: SiGe epi stacks enabled heterojunction bipolar transistors on standard silicon substrates, supporting the high-frequency analogue and mixed-signal device families used in wireline and optical interfaces. IQE's SiGe capability gave it access to device customers operating in the boundary between silicon CMOS and compound semiconductor performance domains.

The VCSEL epi platform — vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser structures, comprising precisely tuned distributed Bragg reflector mirror stacks surrounding a thin quantum-well active region, with an oxide-aperture confinement layer — represented perhaps IQE's most intricate recipe library. VCSEL structures required growth of dozens of alternating semiconductor layers, each held to thickness tolerances tighter than a single nanometre, across the full diameter of 150mm or 200mm wafers. The mirror reflectivity, cavity resonance wavelength, and aperture oxide uniformity all depended on this growth precision. IQE's VCSEL recipe development, intensified during the Apple 3D-sensing supply cycle that peaked around 2017–2019, yielded a process capability and yield record that remained relevant for subsequent VCSEL demand in automotive LiDAR and datacom short-reach interconnect.

## Reactor Estate and Facility Architecture

IQE's production reactor fleet spanned four principal operating sites. Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, housed the largest MOCVD reactor installation in the group and, at peak, was among the highest-capacity compound semiconductor epi facilities globally — a concentration of Aixtron and Veeco production reactors representing capital investment accumulated over the full history of the II-Chel and then IQE operations in North America. Taunton, Massachusetts, brought additional VCSEL-qualified MOCVD capacity when IQE acquired the Kopin Corporation compound semiconductor epi facility in 2018; the Taunton site expanded the group's ability to serve 850nm and 940nm VCSEL customers at production scale without compromising the Bethlehem manufacturing lines. Cardiff retained European production capability and housed a portion of the advanced research and development activity. Singapore served the Asian supply chain, positioning IQE wafer delivery within the logistics perimeter of the Southeast Asian and Taiwan foundry ecosystem.

The geographic distribution of reactor capacity was both a commercial hedge and a customer requirement: major RF amplifier customers running just-in-time supply chains wanted qualified production sites on multiple continents. Maintaining cross-qualified recipes — growth recipes validated to produce equivalent electrical and optical performance on reactors at different facilities — was an ongoing engineering programme that few smaller epi companies could resource.

## Patents, Licensing, and R&D Intensity

IQE's patent portfolio spanned epi growth recipes, process flows, reactor modifications, and aspects of device structure. The breadth of the portfolio reflected decades of incremental process development, with filings clustering around VCSEL mirror stack architectures, GaN buffer engineering, and InP active-region compositions for high-speed photonic devices. The company maintained cross-licensing arrangements with integrated device manufacturers whose in-house epi capability intersected IQE's process IP, converting potential IP disputes into framework agreements that reinforced rather than undermined commercial relationships.

Research and development expenditure ran at a sustained elevated rate relative to revenue, consistent with IQE's characterisation of itself as a technology-led supplier rather than a commodity wafer producer. Annual report disclosures through the early 2020s showed R&D charges representing a meaningful high-single-digit percentage of group revenue — a level of investment that supported simultaneous roadmap development across InP photonics, 5G RF GaN, and emerging applications including automotive LiDAR epi stacks and photonic integrated circuit substrates. The InP roadmap carried particular urgency as 800G optical transceiver designs moved from sampling to volume qualification across hyperscaler procurement programmes; IQE's recipe development pipeline for the device structures underpinning coherent optical interconnect was, by the mid-2020s, the R&D programme most directly connected to the company's medium-term revenue inflection case.

chapters.title: Capacity utilisation, customer concentration, captive-epi competition, capital structure
chapters.body:
## The utilisation trap

IQE's cost structure is defined by its reactors. Each metal-organic chemical vapour deposition tool represents a multi-million pound capital commitment with a fixed depreciation charge that runs regardless of whether wafers are being produced. The company's two principal US facilities — the 200,000 square-foot Bethlehem, Pennsylvania operation and the substantially larger Taunton, Massachusetts mega-facility acquired from Kopin in 2018 — were sized for a demand environment that had not yet fully materialised when revenue peaked at £178 million in 2020 and then contracted sharply to £115.3 million by 2023.

The mathematics are punishing. When epitaxial reactors run at reduced utilisation, fixed depreciation and maintenance costs are spread across a smaller wafer area output, compressing gross margin directly. The Bethlehem facility, which opened as one of the largest compound semiconductor epitaxy operations globally, carried material idle capacity through the 2022–2024 contraction cycle. Taunton, purpose-built for VCSEL and broader photonics production at scale, faced the same structural headwind as Apple's Face ID VCSEL volumes normalised after the 2017–2020 surge. Revenue compression from £178 million in 2020 to £115.3 million in 2023 — a decline of roughly 35 per cent over three years — translated directly into operating losses at the consolidated level.

The near-term mitigant is the InP photonics demand recovery. As AI data centre operators accelerated deployment of 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers, each unit of which consumes meaningful InP epitaxial wafer area, reactor utilisation in IQE's photonics lines was positioned to improve. The medium-term concern is timing: the capital and fixed-cost burden continues to accrue irrespective of when the demand inflection fully arrives at IQE's order book.

## Customer concentration and programme dependency

IQE's revenue base has historically been concentrated among a small number of semiconductor customers. The RF segment leans heavily on the major GaAs power amplifier suppliers — Qorvo, Broadcom, and Skyworks Solutions principal among them — whose output volumes track smartphone production cycles and 5G base station deployment. The photonics segment is similarly concentrated, with Lumentum and Coherent (which absorbed II-VI in 2022) representing the principal downstream consumers of IQE's VCSEL and InP epitaxy.

The practical consequence is that a programme change at a single major customer — a design win reversal, an inventory digestion cycle, or a decision to accelerate in-house epi capability — can move IQE's revenue materially. The Apple VCSEL cycle demonstrated this in both directions: the ramp from 2017 to 2020 as Face ID volume scaled was transformational for IQE's top line; the subsequent normalisation as Apple's supply chain matured and alternative VCSEL suppliers invested in capacity was equally consequential on the downside.

Coherent presents a specific monitoring point. The company is simultaneously a significant IQE customer for photonics epi and a potential captive-epi competitor through its own vertically integrated operations. As Coherent scaled its transceiver manufacturing for AI data centre applications, the allocation between merchant epi supply from IQE and internally grown material remained a variable IQE did not control. Any acceleration of Coherent's captive epi investment would reduce the addressable merchant market for IQE's InP reactor hours.

## Captive epitaxy: the structural competitor

The compound semiconductor industry contains a cohort of integrated device manufacturers that operate their own epitaxial growth capability. Sumitomo Electric, one of the largest InP substrate and epi producers globally, is vertically integrated from crystal growth through device. Coherent, through its inherited II-VI operations, carries internal epi capability. Several Asian compound semiconductor foundries similarly operate captive epi as part of their standard process flows.

The merchant epi model — IQE's entire strategic proposition — rests on the assertion that independent specialists can deliver better material quality, a broader process portfolio, and lower unit cost than IDM captive operations sized for narrower internal demand. That argument holds when merchant volume scale exceeds what any given captive line can justify economically. It weakens when IDMs are growing their own volumes rapidly enough to invest in captive epi that amortises across large internal demand.

The AI photonics inflection creates a structural tension here. If 800G and 1.6T transceiver volumes grow as hyperscaler build-out projections suggest, the largest integrated transceiver suppliers — Coherent, Marvell-Inphi's component partners, and others — will face a make-versus-buy decision on InP epi at a scale that makes captive investment economically attractive. IQE's medium-term competitive position in InP photonics epi depends partly on whether it can execute the volume ramp faster, and at higher yield and lower unit cost, than its customers can build or expand internal alternatives.

## Capital structure and liquidity headroom

IQE remained pre-profit at the consolidated level through the 2022–2024 contraction period, a direct consequence of the utilisation shortfall. The company carried a fixed depreciation load from its US facilities while revenue compressed, producing operating losses that consumed cash. With approximately 600 employees and the fixed infrastructure of multiple large-scale epi facilities, the monthly cash outflow during periods of under-utilisation was substantial.

The board's decision to initiate a CEO succession process in late 2024 — resulting in the departure of Americo Lemos in October of that year — reflected in part the urgency of the operational restructuring required. Lemos had joined from GlobalFoundries in February 2022 with a mandate to professionalise IQE's operations and execute the US facility strategy; his departure after less than three years signalled the board's conclusion that the pace of recovery needed to accelerate.

Cash position and liquidity headroom remained consistent investor concerns through the contraction cycle. The company's ability to fund reactor maintenance, sustain process development investment for InP photonics, and service its capital structure was directly dependent on utilisation recovery. Any further revenue compression — from a 5G RF cycle deterioration, an AI capex pause, or a customer programme cancellation — would tighten an already constrained financial position and potentially force asset or facility decisions that reduce long-term optionality.

## AI photonics execution risk

The forward investment thesis for IQE was substantially predicated on hyperscaler AI infrastructure capital expenditure. The 800G and 1.6T optical transceiver programmes that consume InP epi area were themselves dependent on continued expansion of AI data centre fibre interconnect. Should hyperscaler capex moderate — whether from macro deterioration, AI investment cycle normalisation, or architectural shifts toward co-packaged optics that alter InP epi content per port — the demand pull that justified IQE's InP utilisation thesis would weaken commensurately.

The timing risk was material. IQE's fixed cost base accrued continuously; the InP photonics demand inflection was episodic and customer-programme-dependent. A six-month delay in a major 1.6T transceiver programme launch, or an inventory build-and-digest cycle among optical module manufacturers, translated directly into extended under-utilisation of IQE's InP reactors without a commensurate reduction in fixed costs.

## Substrate supply: the upstream constraint

InP epitaxial wafer production requires InP substrates — polished single-crystal wafers on which the epitaxial layers are grown. The global InP substrate supply base is narrow, dominated by a small number of producers including Sumitomo Electric and AXT. Periodic tightness in InP substrate availability has historically affected IQE's ability to scale output rapidly in response to demand inflections.

As the AI photonics build-out placed accelerating demand on InP epi across the industry, substrate availability and pricing were being tested. IQE did not manufacture its own InP substrates, leaving it exposed to supply constraints that originated upstream in the material supply chain. A substrate shortage — driven either by InP crystal growth capacity limitations or by competing demand from captive IDM epi operations buying ahead of tightness — could constrain IQE's ability to capitalise on the photonics demand inflection even when its own reactors had spare capacity. The substrate cost line also bears directly on epi gross margin; input price inflation in a period of already-compressed utilisation compounds the financial pressure.

## The vicious cycle

The six risks described above are not independent. They interact through a reinforcing dynamic that represents the central structural challenge IQE's management faced as of the snapshot date.

Under-utilisation of Bethlehem and Taunton compresses gross margin and operating cash flow. Constrained cash flow limits capital available for process development investment, reactor upgrades, and talent retention in a highly specialised engineering discipline. Reduced investment capacity weakens IQE's ability to win and retain customer programmes against captive-epi competition and better-capitalised rivals. Weaker programme wins reduce utilisation further, restarting the cycle.

Breaking the loop requires either a demand-side event — InP photonics volume arriving at sufficient scale to drive meaningful utilisation improvement — or an operational rationalisation event, such as a material reduction in the US facility footprint to bring fixed costs into alignment with the revenue base that can realistically be defended. The board's initiation of a CEO succession process in late 2024 suggested an acknowledgment that the operational response needed to be more decisive than it had been. Whether the incoming leadership would pursue facility rationalisation, a demand recovery strategy, or a combination of both remained the defining question for IQE's financial trajectory as the snapshot window closed.

chapters.title: The next 12 months — catalysts, estimates, and what to watch
chapters.body:
## The earnings calendar

The twelve months from May 2026 represent IQE's most consequential testing period since the Apple VCSEL peak of 2020. Steve Smith's first full year as permanent chief executive closes with the company's half-year results in September 2026, and the thesis that InP photonics can structurally replace lost VCSEL volume — and that 5G RF has genuinely troughed — will be validated or falsified by a handful of specific data points across four reporting events.

**Annual General Meeting, June 2026.** The 2026 AGM, anticipated in the first half of June, will carry a trading update or interim management statement. The market will focus on any revenue guidance language for full-year 2026 and on commentary about InP order cadence from data centre transceiver customers. Smith's tone at his first AGM as permanent chief executive will be read as a signal of confidence.

**Half-year 2026 interim results, September 2026.** The H1 reporting event is the next hard number. The prior-year comparator — H1 2025 — sets the baseline against which analysts calibrate FY2026 consensus. Critically, this report will carry gross margin data for the first six months, which is the single most important operating metric for a business restructuring around under-utilised fixed capacity in Bethlehem and Taunton.

**FY2026 preliminary results, March 2027.** The full-year print, arriving approximately nine to ten months from the snapshot date, is the culminating event of the twelve-month window. Analyst consensus for FY2026 will converge as the year progresses; any beat or miss against that consensus will have been substantially telegraphed by the September 2026 H1 data.

**Ad hoc RNS announcements.** IQE has historically issued trading updates, capital markets day communications, and major contract announcements via London Stock Exchange RNS between scheduled results. Any significant customer win — particularly an InP design win with a hyperscaler-linked transceiver manufacturer — would appear here first and carry immediate re-rating implications.

## What the recovery consensus prices in

IQE's revenue troughed at £115.3 million in 2023 — the sharpest contraction since the business passed through the post-dot-com normalisation — against a cycle peak of £178 million in 2020. The sell-side consensus at the May 2026 snapshot, covered principally by [Berenberg](https://www.berenberg.de), [Canaccord Genuity](https://www.canaccordgenuity.com), and [Peel Hunt](https://www.peelhunt.com), reflected an expectation that the 2023 floor was a structural trough rather than a new base, with recovery driven by two distinct vectors: a return to volume in 5G RF GaAs wafers as Qorvo, Broadcom, and Skyworks restocked supply chains that had been deliberately drawn down through 2022 and 2023; and the emerging InP photonics ramp tied to 800G and 1.6T optical transceiver demand at hyperscale data centres.

| Metric | Recovery consensus expectation | Signal threshold |
|---|---|---|
| Group revenue | Path toward £140–160m on the multi-year recovery arc | H1 2026 organic growth rate vs. prior-year H1 |
| Gross margin | Expansion toward 25–30% as US facility utilisation recovers | ≥25% in H1 2026 confirms US plant absorption |
| InP revenue mix | InP photonics growing as a share of group revenue above 15–20% | Segmental disclosure or explicit management commentary |
| Net debt / cash | Trajectory toward balance sheet stability, no dilutive equity raise required | Net cash / (debt) line in half-year accounts |

IQE does not provide quarterly segmental revenue guidance on the US model. The company's disclosures run on a semi-annual basis, compressing information frequency relative to NASDAQ-listed peers such as Coherent or Lumentum. This structural opacity is a source of volatility: each half-year print carries information that has been building for six months, and the bid-offer spread on the stock typically widens materially in the weeks before each results date.

## Management guidance: the qualitative frame

Smith, who joined IQE as permanent chief executive in early 2025 following the October 2024 departure of Americo Lemos, positioned the business around three execution priorities on taking office: restoring gross margin through disciplined capacity utilisation; capturing the InP photonics demand inflection; and maintaining 5G RF customer relationships as that market recovers from its 2022–2023 inventory trough. In IQE's [FY2025 preliminary results](https://www.iqep.com/investors/) and subsequent communications, the company signalled confidence in the photonics trajectory without providing specific revenue targets — consistent with IQE's longstanding practice of qualitative rather than numerical guidance.

The market consequently reads management language with close attention to tonal signal: references to "design win momentum," "increasing customer qualification activity," or "capacity commitments" are treated as forward indicators by the sell-side coverage universe. Absence of such language — or hedging language around "slower-than-expected qualification timelines" — carries equivalent weight in the other direction.

## The four data points to watch each reporting period

**InP revenue growth, absolute and relative.** The entire bull thesis rests on InP epitaxy becoming a meaningful revenue vector as optical transceiver manufacturers ramp 800G production for AI data centre buildouts. If H1 2026 results carry explicit InP revenue growth disclosure, or management commentary citing accelerating customer qualification pipelines, that confirms the structural inflection that the [LightCounting](https://lightcounting.com) optical interconnect market data had been pointing toward through 2025. Neutral language is the bear signal; silence is worse.

**Gross margin trajectory.** IQE's gross margin is a direct function of epi reactor utilisation across its Bethlehem and Taunton US facilities, which carried excess capacity through the 2022–2024 trough. A gross margin above 25% in H1 2026 would signal that utilisation has recovered to the level where the fixed-cost base is being absorbed. A gross margin below 20% would indicate the US facilities remain significantly under-loaded and damage the multi-year recovery narrative.

**Cash generation and balance sheet.** IQE navigated the trough period with recourse to credit facilities. Any RNS announcement before September 2026 disclosing a material debt facility renewal, equity placing, or covenant discussion would be a negative catalyst of the first order — signalling that the recovery is not generating the cash conversion management had guided.

**RF customer lead indicators.** Qorvo, Broadcom, and Skyworks collectively represent IQE's largest revenue exposure through their GaAs power amplifier demand. All three publish quarterly earnings in the months before and after IQE's half-year results. Their guidance language on GaAs wafer purchase volumes and supply chain restocking provides a lead indicator for IQE's RF revenue in H2 2026 that is available to the market weeks before IQE's own reporting.

## Beat versus miss: the thresholds

A **beat** against the May 2026 consensus would require at least two of the following in the September 2026 H1 results: revenue ahead of the prior H1 by a margin exceeding analyst estimates; gross margin at or above 25%; explicit disclosure of new InP customer qualifications or volume commitments from a named transceiver manufacturer; and net cash or reduced net debt relative to the December 2025 year-end balance sheet.

A **miss** would be triggered by any single one of: revenue growth below the prior-year H1 run-rate, implying the recovery is stalling; gross margin compression below 20%, signalling renewed US facility underloading; balance sheet deterioration requiring new funding; or management language that qualifies InP momentum with references to "slower-than-expected" customer qualification timelines.

## The bull and bear asymmetry

The bull setup is structurally compelling. InP epitaxy is not readily substitutable: the capital intensity of compound semiconductor epi reactors, the qualification cycles that run twelve to eighteen months, and IQE's status as the principal independent epi supplier create a near-term supply oligopoly in InP as AI data centre optical interconnect demand scales through the 800G-to-1.6T transition wave. If the InP volume growth that optical interconnect analysts were projecting through 2025 delivers into IQE's order book, revenue recovery toward the £160–175 million range by 2027 — approaching the prior cycle peak of £178 million — would imply gross margin recovery that, on current fixed costs, generates a meaningfully different earnings profile from the trough years. The stock, trading near multi-year lows at the snapshot date, prices in very little of this scenario.

The bear case carries equal structural validity. IQE has disappointed recovery expectations before: the 2022 revenue of £167 million gave way to the 2023 trough of £115.3 million faster than sell-side models had projected. The US facility cost base remains a structural drag in any scenario where utilisation fails to recover. The CEO transition carries execution risk: Smith's priorities are clearly stated but unproven in terms of delivery at scale. And the InP demand inflection, while structurally real, is mediated through Lumentum, Coherent, and Marvell-Inphi — customers who themselves carry their own inventory and capacity cycles. A slowdown in hyperscaler capital expenditure would propagate directly into IQE's InP order book with limited buffer.

The asymmetry at the May 2026 snapshot favours the bull case on a twelve-month horizon, conditional on InP qualification momentum holding and on Smith delivering the gross margin recovery his first full-year results must evidence by March 2027. The margin of safety is the compressed valuation; the binary swing factor is execution.

chapters.title: The InP-photonics-led recovery scenario and the InP-substrate question
chapters.body:
## The InP demand thesis: structure and preconditions

By the time IQE's board moved to replace chief executive Americo Lemos in October 2024, the strategic thesis for the company's recovery had already crystallised around a single material: indium phosphide. The revenue trajectory that had carried IQE from £140m in 2019 to £178m at the Apple VCSEL peak in 2020 — before falling back to £115.3m in 2023 — traced the arc of the consumer 3D-sensing cycle almost exactly. The next potential inflection, in the view the company communicated to shareholders through 2023 and 2024, would trace a different cycle entirely: the scaling of high-speed optical interconnect inside artificial intelligence data centres.

The structural logic is straightforward. As hyperscalers — Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon and their infrastructure peers — assembled AI training clusters of increasing density, the optical transceiver volume required to interconnect GPU and accelerator nodes grew with it. Each 800 Gigabit-per-second transceiver, the dominant standard entering commercial deployment through 2024, and each emerging 1.6 Terabit-per-second device consuming InP epi area substantially larger than a comparable silicon-based equivalent, meant that aggregate InP epitaxial wafer demand scaled in approximate proportion to the number of transceivers shipped into those clusters. IQE, as the principal merchant supplier of InP epi wafers, occupied the foundational layer of that supply chain.

## The InP epi supply chain and IQE's position in it

The manufacture of a high-speed optical transceiver for datacentre interconnect begins with a substrate — typically an InP substrate wafer grown by a specialist substrate house — onto which IQE and a small number of competitors deposit epitaxial layers using metal-organic chemical vapour deposition reactors. Those epi wafers then pass to a device fabricator, who patterns and processes them into laser, modulator or photodetector chips. Those chips are integrated into transceiver modules by companies including Lumentum, Coherent (formerly II-VI) and Marvell-Inphi's optical division, before entering the hyperscaler's procurement chain.

IQE's position — as the epi supplier rather than the device maker or module assembler — means its economics are governed primarily by epi wafer area shipped and the utilisation of its MOCVD reactor capacity. The Bethlehem, Pennsylvania facility, at approximately 200,000 square feet one of the largest compound semiconductor epi installations globally at the time of its opening, carried substantial idle capacity through the 2022-2024 period following the post-VCSEL volume correction. The Taunton, Massachusetts mega-facility, originally the Kopin compound semiconductor campus acquired by IQE in 2018, added further scale that the post-Apple demand compression had left underutilised.

The central operating leverage question as the snapshot date approached was therefore not whether InP photonics demand from AI data centres was real — by 2024 and into 2025, the transceiver industry's own order signals were sufficiently clear — but whether IQE could absorb a sufficient share of that demand to bring its fixed cost base into sustainable coverage.

## The 5G RF floor: modest recovery, not a second peak

Alongside the InP photonics thesis, IQE continued to maintain a significant revenue exposure to the 5G radio-frequency market through GaAs epitaxial wafer supply into the power amplifier supply chain serving customers including Qorvo, Broadcom and Skyworks Solutions. That market, which had contributed meaningfully to IQE's 2019-2022 revenue base, entered a period of more subdued dynamics after the 2020-2021 peak in handset bill-of-materials intensity.

The 5G handset cycle that unfolded through 2023 and 2024 was structurally more moderate than the initial deployment surge. Carrier capital expenditure in the principal markets — the United States, Europe and Japan — had passed its most aggressive build-out phase. China's 5G infrastructure rollout, which had been a significant demand driver for base station RF GaAs, continued at a pace governed by domestic carriers' own investment cycles, which proved more variable than initial industry forecasts implied.

For IQE, the 5G RF segment provided a base load of GaAs epi volume that could not be counted upon to deliver step-change revenue growth from the 2023-2024 level. The realistic expectation, as articulated through management communications, was cyclical stabilisation rather than a new peak. Recovery in carrier capex and a return of handset upgrade intensity following the post-COVID inventory correction provided some tailwind, but the RF GaAs segment's contribution to IQE's medium-term recovery scenario was supportive rather than primary.

## VCSEL: automotive LiDAR's promise and its present scale

The third leg of IQE's epi portfolio, the VCSEL business, underwent its own structural reset following the normalisation of the Apple Face ID volume that had driven the 2017-2020 surge. The company retained VCSEL epi production capability at its Taunton facility and continued to serve customers including Coherent and AMS-OSRAM across sensing and datacom applications.

Automotive LiDAR represented the forward growth narrative for VCSEL at the snapshot date, with automotive OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers advancing ADAS and autonomous driving sensor systems that relied on VCSEL array illumination. The technology scaling was genuine. But the absolute volumes reachable by automotive LiDAR through the 2025-2027 horizon remained, in aggregate, smaller than the historical consumer 3D-sensing volumes at their peak. The transition from hundreds of millions of smartphones to tens of millions of vehicles — each carrying a fraction of the array density required for a smartphone Face ID module — shaped the unit economics of automotive VCSEL demand in ways that bounded its near-term contribution to IQE's revenue.

Datacom VCSELs, used in short-reach optical interconnect inside data centres at 850nm wavelengths, provided a complementary demand base that benefited modestly from the same AI infrastructure build-out driving InP transceiver demand, but at lower aggregate epi content per transceiver than InP long-reach variants.

## Operational posture under new leadership

The CEO transition that placed IQE's operational steering in interim hands through the latter part of 2024 and into the succession process that followed represented a board-level signal that the pace of restructuring required acceleration. The facility footprint assembled during the VCSEL-era expansion — Bethlehem at 200,000 square feet, Taunton at mega-facility scale, Cardiff as headquarters and primary European operations, with further capacity in Singapore and the Taiwan joint venture — had been sized for a revenue base materially above £115.3m. Operating that footprint at the 2023 revenue level generated the utilisation drag that compressed gross margins and sustained losses at the operating line.

The incoming leadership's mandate, as legible from board communications and investor statements through the period, was to right-size the operational cost base to the achievable near-term revenue envelope while preserving the epi capacity required to capture the InP photonics upswing when transceiver customer pull-through materialised at scale. Jutta Meier, as CFO providing continuity through the transition, held the balance sheet discipline through a period in which the company's cash position and liquidity headroom required active management.

## Capital structure: the liquidity constraint

IQE's capital structure entering 2025 reflected the cumulative cash consumption of the VCSEL-era capacity build and the subsequent years of losses on underutilised facilities. The company's ability to navigate the period before InP photonics revenue scaled to fixed-cost-covering levels depended on maintaining adequate liquidity headroom — either through operating cash generation from existing revenue, from any available debt facilities, or from capital market access. The prospect of equity issuance, as a mechanism for balance sheet repair if cash burn continued, carried dilution risk for existing shareholders and represented a monitoring variable for investors through the period.

## Risks in the recovery scenario

| Risk factor | Mechanism | Current read |
|---|---|---|
| Capacity utilisation | Fixed-cost drag persists below ~£140m revenue | Remains operative at 2023 revenue level |
| Customer concentration | Lumentum, Coherent, Qorvo together represent dominant revenue share | Structural feature, not easily diversified |
| Captive epi competition | Vertically-integrated device makers (Coherent) developing in-house epi | Ongoing; limits merchant market addressable share |
| Capital structure | Liquidity headroom under continued losses | Active risk; management under active attention |
| InP substrate bottleneck | InP substrate supply (AXT, Wafer Technology) a parallel constraint on epi output | Industry-level, not IQE-specific |

## The central question

The chapter's analytical core reduces to a single question: does the InP photonics demand pull from AI data centre optical interconnect translate into IQE merchant InP epi revenue at scale, and does that revenue absorb the fixed cost base sufficiently to deliver structural profitability?

The constructive case rests on three pillars that were, by the snapshot date, each individually credible. First, the AI data centre optical interconnect build-out was real and durable, with hyperscaler capital expenditure guidance through 2024 and 2025 pointing to sustained cluster-scale investment. Second, InP epi content per 800G and 1.6T transceiver was measurably larger than prior-generation 100G and 400G devices, meaning the same transceiver unit growth implied disproportionately greater epi area demand. Third, IQE retained the reactor capacity and process capability — accumulated through the VCSEL-era investment — to serve InP epi demand without a capital-intensive new build.

The risks that qualified that case were equally concrete. Captive epi development by vertically-integrated customers such as Coherent represented the most structurally durable headwind: a customer that brought epi in-house was a customer permanently removed from IQE's merchant addressable market. The substrate question — whether InP substrate supply from AXT, Wafer Technology and others would scale in parallel with epi demand, or create a bottleneck that constrained overall transceiver output — sat upstream of IQE in the value chain but shaped the total available volume. And the timing question — whether InP photonics revenue would reach fixed-cost-covering scale before the liquidity runway required fresh capital — remained the most immediate variable governing the investment case.

As of 23 May 2026, the thesis had not yet been resolved. IQE stood at the intersection of a structurally favourable demand pull and a structurally demanding operational position, with the outcome dependent on the pace of transceiver demand conversion into epi purchase orders, the discipline of cost restructuring under new leadership, and the durability of the merchant InP epi market against captive competition. The equipment and the capability were in place. The question was whether the volumes would arrive in time.

## Appendix C — Product and Material System Categories

**Gallium arsenide (GaAs):** Principal material for 5G RF power amplifiers and microwave devices. Primary volume driver from smartphone RF content and base station infrastructure.

**Indium phosphide (InP):** High-speed optical interconnect applications — fibre-optic transceivers, telecom and datacom photonics. Emerging demand inflection from AI data centre optical interconnect at 800G and 1.6T.

**Gallium nitride (GaN):** Power electronics and RF applications, including defence and base station.

**VCSEL (Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Laser) epi wafers:** 3D sensing arrays (Apple Face ID legacy), automotive LiDAR, short-reach datacom optical.

**Silicon-germanium (SiGe):** High-speed electronic applications.

## Appendix F — Competitive References

**Sumitomo Electric (Japan):** Large captive epi operations primarily serving internal device divisions; not a true merchant competitor but a benchmark for integrated scale.

**Visual Photonics Epitaxy (Taiwan):** Taiwan-based merchant epi supplier; competes in GaAs and InP for Asian foundry customers.

**Landmark Optoelectronics (Taiwan):** Merchant epi competitor with exposure to photonics and datacom wafer demand.

**Coherent and AMS-OSRAM:** Both operate captive epi capacity for VCSEL and photonic device production, reducing their dependence on IQE for portions of their wafer needs.
